summary: Source-level restructuring, 1.736x (240 pairs, CI 1.730-1.744; 0.209 ms -> 0.120 ms, headroom 1.87 -> 1.07). The baseline reads S twice (predict pass, then update pass) with one strided dword per thread per wait; this was the "re-reads a tensor" case, so reading once was the lever. The winning state reads S once: each of 256 threads owns a 4-column x 16-row tile (x4 loads, 8 rows in flight), decays it, parks the decayed S of the whole head in a 76.8 KB LDS pool and writes a partial pred to LDS; after a barrier the threads sum the partials, apply the delta rule from LDS, store S once, and reduce partial outputs through LDS. Shapes that do not fit the pool (dk*dv + 16*dv > 19200 floats, or dv < 4) take the original two-pass code; column tails are handled by overlapping the last 4-column group (safe because phase 1 only reads global S and phase 2 only writes it). Results are within the manifest tolerance, not bit-identical (pred and out are summed in 8 partials). No machine-IR edits were made on top; amdclang's output passed static_check as is.

friction: static_check rejects amdclang's own output for the two-pass source states (e848ab2ce8326112 .LBB0_18[0] and .LBB0_40[0] `global_load_dwordx4 v[8:11], v[6:7], off offset:-8`: 'overwrites v10 before the memory operation that writes it has completed'; same in a46ae04f95cf480e .LBB0_23[1], .Lft16[5]). Either the checker is stricter than the hardware/compiler here (dead load result overwritten by a later in-order load) or amdclang emits something questionable; fix_waits repaired it, but a source state that fails static with compiler-emitted code deserves a clearer message or an automatic fix_waits.

`source` needs the full text on every call even when only `defines`, `flags` or `launch` change: a 100-line source was resent 6 times for a parameter sweep. A `source(sha=..., defines=...)` or `resource(state, defines, launch)` form would make sweeps cheap.

-D macros named U or W collide with HIP headers (template parameter names in amd_hip_vector_types.h) because defines are applied before the includes; the error is a wall of header diagnostics. A warning for single-letter define names would help.

LDS size is fixed at compile time while the shapes are dynamic: the LDS-parked design needs a fallback path for shapes that do not fit, and the battery only exercises that fallback with DV=1. A way to state shape bounds in the manifest (or a launch-time LDS size expression usable from source) would make this cleaner.

features/bench do not show how many workgroups fit per CU given the LDS allocation; I found the 80 KB cliff (163840 / 2) only by measuring 1.21x vs 1.60x. Occupancy reporting should include the LDS-per-CU limit on concurrent workgroups.
No tool to see the true traffic (bytes actually read per run); the traffic model's 'touched once' assumption hid that the baseline reads S twice until the source was read.
lessons: kda_step: the baseline read the 268 MB state twice (predict pass + update pass). Keeping two passes but with x4 loads, contiguous rows and 4-8 loads in flight gave only 1.07-1.12x; reading S once by parking the intermediate in LDS gave 1.60-1.74x (headroom 1.87 -> 1.07). When a kernel needs a full reduction over a tile before it can update it, park the tile in LDS (64 KB here) rather than re-reading global memory.

LDS size sets workgroups per CU: 79.9 KB LDS (2 workgroups per CU) ran at 1.60x, the same design at 85 KB (1 workgroup per CU, even with 512 threads) only 1.21x. Keep LDS at or below 163840 / n bytes for the n concurrent workgroups you want.
With a 64 KB LDS tile per workgroup, more waves per workgroup pay up to 4: block 128 1.46x, block 256 1.60x, block 512 (2 columns per thread) 1.64x = parity with block 256 in a direct compare.

Loads in flight still paid on top of the single-read design: 8 x4 loads per wait instead of 4 gave 1.047x (compare, CI 1.037-1.057), with 114 VGPRs and no spills under -fno-slp-vectorize -fno-vectorize.

Without -fno-slp-vectorize amdclang turned a 4-column x 8-row batch into v_pk_* code with 128 VGPRs and 20 scratch spills; it was nonetheless faster (1.12x) than the clean 4-row version (1.07x), so the batch size mattered more than the spills in that two-pass variant.

Overlapping the last column group (c = min(c, dv - 4)) handles column tails without scalar code when reads and writes of the in-out tensor are separated by a barrier (phase 1 only reads global, phase 2 only writes), since duplicated work writes identical values.
Linear accumulators split over 8 row parts and summed through LDS after a barrier passed the battery at rtol 1e-4 (105 cases).

session.final:
`kda_step` now runs **1.736x** faster than amdclang's build (0.209 ms → 0.120 ms, 240 pairs, CI 1.730–1.744), and the state `e15d5e8f5d212aaf` passes the static check and the full 105-case battery. The report is recorded with that state as best.

- **Which case this was:** the baseline re-reads a tensor. It reads the 268 MB state `S` twice (predict pass, then update pass), so reading it once was the lever. Reference headroom was 1.87; the winning state sits at 1.07, close to the memory floor.
- **What the winner does:** it reads `S` once and parks the decayed copy of the head in LDS (79.9 KB). Each of 256 threads owns a 4-column × 16-row tile with 8 wide loads in flight. After a barrier it applies the delta rule from LDS and writes `S` once.
- **Shapes that don't fit:** anything that overflows the LDS pool, or has `DV` < 4, takes the original two-pass code. The battery only exercises that fallback with `DV` = 1.
- **Not bit-identical:** `pred` and `out` are summed in 8 partials, so results are within the manifest tolerance rather than equal to the baseline's.

| Variant | Speedup |
|---|---|
| Two passes kept, wide loads, 4 rows in flight | 1.07x |
| Two passes kept, wide loads, 8 rows in flight | 1.12x |
| Single read via LDS, block 128 | 1.46x |
| Single read via LDS, block 256, 4 rows in flight | 1.60x |
| Single read via LDS, block 512, 2 columns per thread | 1.64x (parity with block 256 in a direct compare) |
| Single read via LDS, block 512, LDS at 85 KB | 1.21x |
| **Single read via LDS, block 256, 8 rows in flight** | **1.74x** |

The 85 KB result is the main trap: above 80 KB only one workgroup fits per compute unit, and the same design loses most of its gain.

I made no machine-IR edits on the winner and stopped after 9 timed candidates. Two friction items worth acting on:

- `static_check` rejected amdclang's own output for the two-pass variants until `fix_waits` was applied.
- `source` needs the full text resent for every parameter sweep.
